mentions.name: ADB Remote
mentions.description: ADB Remote wraps common ADB and Gradle operations into a single interface so Android development tasks can be done without launching Android Studio. It includes a file explorer to open project files in an editor, Git operations to checkout and run any branch/tag directly on a device, Gradle task execution (assembleDebug, installDebug, custom tasks) with streaming output, a live Logcat viewer with filtering by level/tag/search, a foreground activity tracker, ADB device tools (clear data, uninstall, manage permissions, input text, screenshots), screenshot-comparison visual testing to catch UI regressions, and terminal integration with iTerm2, Terminal, Warp, and others.
mentions.problem: Doing quick Android development tasks requires committing to launching the heavyweight Android Studio; this tool lets developers handle common ADB and Gradle operations in a lighter single interface.
mentions.audience: Android developers, especially those who avoid Android Studio for quick device tasks
mentions.source_excerpt:
I'm building ADB Remote from the sole desire to be able to do Android development without having to commit to launching Android Studio.
ADB Remote wraps common ADB and Gradle operations into a single interface.
